original_question: Is Peutz–Jeghers syndrome a genetic disorder associated with gene variants on non-sex chromosomes?

final_qi.question: Is Peutz–Jeghers syndrome a genetic disorder associated with gene variants on non-sex chromosomes?
final_qi.long_answer: Peutz–Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an inherited disease characterized by mucocutaneous pigmentation and multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps. The disorder is classically transmitted in an autosomal-dominant fashion and is most commonly caused by pathogenic variants in the STK11 (also called LKB1) tumor-suppressor gene. STK11 is situated on chromosome 19p13.3, which is an autosome (a non-sex chromosome). Therefore, PJS is indeed a genetic disorder linked to variants on a non-sex chromosome, satisfying the description given in the question.
